newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco's bourse ends 0.40 pct lower.
newsitem.headline: Morocco's bourse ends 0.40 pct lower.

text.p: Casablanca stock exchange ended on Monday 0.40 percent lower following nearly two weeks of downward corrections, but there were gains mainly in energy firms, traders said.
The all-share index closed at 663.97 points from 666.61 on Friday.
"The market pursues a quiet trading with a strong demand notably for oil refinery Samir and Societe Cherifiennes des Petroles," a broker at ABN-AMRO Finance said.
ONA Group, Morocco's largest private conglomerate, fell 10 dirhams to 790 dirhams with 4,244 shares traded.
SNI, the second largest private conglomerate edged up one dirham to 726 dirhams with 6,743 shares exchanged.
Steel mill Sonasid dropped 14 dirhams to 551 dirhams.
Cement firm Lafarge Ciments dipped 39 dirhams to 1,276 dirhams.
Ciments de l'Oriental fell 20 dirhams to 649 dirhams.
In the banking sector, Banque Commerciale du Maroc, shed 14 dirhams to 850 dirhams.

Among good performers were Samir, which gained 11.3 dirhams to 388.50 dirhams, Societe Cherifienne des Petroles up 74 dirhams to 762 dirhams with only 16 shares traded and Leasing firm Maroc-Leasing which rose 13 dirhams to 469 dirhams.
Total traded volume on the official market was 37.9 million dirhams from 32.1 million on Friday.
Volume on the official market was 16 million dirhams from 186.2 million dirhams on Friday, a bourse official said.
